11481
Explosibility of carbonaceous dusts.
Dust explosion data obtained in laboratory studies are presented for activated carbon, asphalt, charcoal, carbon black, coal, coke, gilsonite, graphite, lignite, miscellaneous carbons, pitch, tunnel dust, and mixtures of these materials with other ingredients. The explosion hazard is shown to increase as the volatile content of the dusts increases.

Summary of underground coal mine fires : January 1, 1970 to December 31, 1977

9768
Beneficiation of a Hematitic Taconite by Reduction Roasting, Magnetic Separation, and Flotation
The Bureau of Mines has undertaken beneficiation investigations on samples representing large tonnages of oxidized taconites in order to develop and evaluate applicable technologies for producing iron oxide concentrates from these materials. Information derived from the investigations can be used to expand the domestic iron raw-materials base and to establish the impact these taconite deposits may have on future national iron ore requirements. This report describes a process that includes reduction roasting, magnetic separation, and flotation, applied to a western Mesabi Range sample taken near Coleraine, Minn. The sample contained 36.8 pct iron and 46.0 pct silica, and represented 0.5 to 1 billion tons of crude material. An average of 962 Ib/hr of oxidized taconite was roasted with 33 Ib/hr of lignite in a 35-foot-long rotary kiln. Pulverized lignite and natural gas maintained the kiln operating temperature at 850? C. The roasted taconite was beneficiated by magnetic separation and cationic flotation in a 900-lb/hr pilot plant and yielded a product analyzing 68.1 pct iron and 4.6 pct silica, and containing 82.4 pct of the iron in the kiln feed.

An Engineering Evaluation of the Fire and Explosion Hazards at 2 Cement Plants and 2 Lime Plants
This report will present a general discussion of coal characteristics and of pulverized fuel systems. However, this report is primarily intended to provide an engineering evaluation of each of the four plants visited; pertaining to their everyday operations and the possible fire and explosion hazards that may exist. Along these lines, recommendations will be provided regarding each specific plant, Finally, information and recommendations will be provided pertaining to fire detection and suppression methods that are currently in use at pulverized fuel systems around the country

9506
Recent Rock-Dusting Experiments for Arresting Coal-Mine Explosions
This report describes an investigation in an Experimental coal mine aat Bruceton, Pa., to determine the efficacy and safety of dispersing rock dust by explosives and to ascertain whether explosive gas-air mixtures or coal dust might be ignited during this rock dusting. It also describes some recent experiments on bag-tyoe devices in which each unit was provided with a burster for scattering rock dust in the path of the explosion.
United States. Bureau of Mines.

9432
Use of Salts to Allay Dust on Shuttle-Car Roadways in Coal Mines
This report discusses how flaked calcium chloride or unrefined, granular sodium chloride applied to shuttle car roadways in normally humid coal mines allays dust effectively. When these salts are properly used and maintained, loose material in the roadway is thoroughly wetted and consolidated, providing a good pavement for traffic. It is emphasized that it is still necessary to combat explosion hazard of coal dust that clings to roof, ribs, and timber surfaces by rock dusting.
United States. Bureau of Mines.
